title: TDS takes a second win in three at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Pierre Thiriet and Mathias Beche won by 21 seconds in the #1 Thiriet by TDS Oreca after pole-sitting Jota took a stop-go and Murphy lost 20 laps.

chapters.title: A crucial middle round in the Alps
text: The 3 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 20 July 2013 was the third of five European Le Mans Series rounds, and the middle one, so it carried real weight in the championship. Thiriet by TDS Racing arrived as leader after a season of contrasts: a strategic call to pit under the safety car had cost the team the win at Silverstone, where Jota Sport's Simon Dolan and Oliver Turvey won the opener, before a deserved victory at Imola. Morand Racing came fresh from fifth place at Le Mans and a Silverstone with no points, and its principal Benoît Morand spoke openly of chasing a podium with seven fast cars in the class.

The entry shifted in the week before the race. Greaves Motorsport withdrew its Zytek on Tuesday after a sponsor changed its plans late, the first time the team had missed a European ACO-rules race since it started in 2006, and DKR Engineering's Lola never turned up in Austria. Murphy Prototypes had Jonathan Hirschi alongside Brendon Hartley, as Mark Patterson was not on the entry, while Boutsen Ginion Racing gave Lotus WEC drivers Dominik Kraihamer and Thomas Holzer the wheel of its Oreca #4, the Austrian Kraihamer racing at home. The biggest newcomer was SMP Racing, which added an Oreca-Judd #37 for Maurizio Mediani and Serguey Zlobin after a decision on the car that came only a couple of weeks earlier.

The weekend itself was an odd one. The ELMS ran as a tag-on to the World Series by Renault meeting, and with the Renault cars in the pit lane the Le Mans teams worked from awnings in the paddock. Any repair beyond routine meant pushing the car through the paddock after notifying race control, a set-up many teams disliked. Temperatures stayed around 30 degrees. In Friday practice Turvey was missing from the first session because he was at a Formula One young-driver test at Silverstone, leaving Dolan to run the whole hour. Mathias Beche's 1:25.638 put the TDS Oreca on top before Patric Niederhauser's 1:24.710 in the Race Performance Oreca led the second session, with Turvey third fastest in the Jota Zytek.

chapters.title: Jota and Murphy on the front row
text: The prototypes had a 20-minute session from 10:50 on Saturday morning, after the GT classes. All eight LMP2 runners were out in the final ten minutes and the first laps quicker than Friday came from Franck Mailleux's Morand Morgan. Brendon Hartley then went to the top for Murphy Prototypes with a 1:24.418 before improving to 1:24.010, and called it a morning with five minutes left.

Turvey, with only three minutes remaining, topped the order with a 1:23.871 in the Jota Zytek #38, and that stood as pole. Hartley took the other front-row slot, Mathias Beche was third on 1:24.054 for TDS, and Mailleux fourth on 1:24.318. Patric Niederhauser put the Race Performance Oreca fifth, ahead of Kraihamer in the Boutsen Ginion Oreca and Mediani in the new SMP car on 1:25.865; the first six were covered by little more than a second.

The Signatech Alpine #36 ran on Michelins while the rest of the prototype field used Dunlops, and Nelson Panciatici's late charge in the final sector made it one of the quickest cars of the session, but Jota, Murphy and TDS filled the top three places on the grid.

chapters.title: Murphy loses its race at the first stop
text: The race started at 16:30 under a clear sky. Hirschi put the early part of Murphy's difficult season behind him with a strong opening stint and ran with Turvey at the head of the field, while Mailleux got into a duel with Beche behind them, finally getting past the TDS Oreca around twenty minutes in. Further back the SMP Oreca was understandably off the pace of the established cars, and the Alpine and the Boutsen Ginion Oreca spent long stretches stuck behind it; the Alpine made its way through after about half an hour, and Kraihamer took longer still.

Murphy's afternoon fell apart at the first routine pit stop. The Oreca refused to restart and had to be taken back to the awning, the same trouble as at Imola, and the car lost 20 laps before it rejoined and eventually finished 25th. Around 40 minutes in Niederhauser went past Beche, and it briefly looked as though the TDS season might be unravelling, but a good first stop put Beche back in front.

chapters.title: Turvey's stop-go and a lost chance for Race Performance
text: After the first round of stops Beche was back in second, with Niederhauser only about two seconds adrift. Around half distance Jota took a stop-go penalty, which dropped Turvey to fourth, 36 seconds behind the leader once the penalty was served. That left the fight for the lead between Beche and Niederhauser, with Mailleux a further 14 seconds back.

It was the Race Performance Oreca that paid next. Niederhauser handed over to Michel Frey, who touched the RAM Racing Ferrari #53 at the final corner and stopped at the side of the track, losing valuable time. Pierre Thiriet took over the TDS car, lost around 12 seconds when it was slow to fire up, and still came out with a lead of some 32 seconds. Dolan, meanwhile, took over the Jota in fifth place and struggled for a lap or two until he had temperature in the tyres. The Boutsen Ginion Oreca's afternoon ended in the second half of the race, stopping after 69 laps without being classified.

chapters.title: Alpine closes in, Dolan takes fourth
text: Thiriet's lead stood at around 32 seconds after the change and was never under serious threat. The man closing it was Panciatici: with roughly 70 minutes to go he took the Alpine past the Morand Morgan for second after several laps of dicing with Natacha Gachnang, and then began to eat into the deficit, cutting it to 21 seconds by the flag.

The best of the remaining fighting was for fourth. Dolan and Frey ran close for much of the closing hour, and with 49 minutes remaining the Englishman went through at the Rindt corner as Frey lost momentum behind a backmarker, a move that settled the place for the Jota. There was very little on-track incident all afternoon, which surprised many drivers given the talk beforehand of cars of every class running at similar speeds and braking at the same points: the Frey contact was the only notable coming together.

chapters.title: Thiriet wins by 21 seconds
text: Thiriet by TDS Racing took the chequered flag after 122 laps, completing a race that lasted 3:00:09.351, 21.143 seconds clear of Ragues and Panciatici in the Alpine. Morand Racing completed the same 122 laps for the second podium in as many rounds, Gachnang and Mailleux 49.915 seconds behind the winner. The three cars on the overall podium were the same three as at Imola.

Jota's Dolan and Turvey were a lap down in fourth in the Zytek, with Race Performance's Niederhauser and Frey, who had been in contention for second before the Frey incident, fifth on the same lap. SMP Racing's new Oreca, Mediani and Zlobin, finished sixth, 119 laps and three down on the winner. Murphy's Hartley and Hirschi, 20 laps down after the long delay at the first stop, were classified 25th, while Boutsen Ginion Racing's Kraihamer and Holzer were the only LMP2 car not classified.

chapters.title: A fast break for the leaders
text: The win gave Thiriet by TDS Racing two victories from the first three rounds and a bigger lead in the championship going into the summer break. Pierre Thiriet and Mathias Beche had again avoided the setbacks that hit their rivals: Jota's stop-go penalty, Murphy's failed restart and the lost minutes at Race Performance, even if their own car was slow to fire up after its stop.

For those who lost out, the afternoon was a case of what might have been. Niederhauser said that if the Frey incident had not happened he thought second for Race Performance would have been certain and a win possible, while stressing that this was an endurance race and such things happen. Murphy Prototypes had little to show for a strong qualifying and a quick first stint, while Alpine finished second, 21 seconds short of the winner.

SMP Racing used the weekend to introduce its new prototype, with Zlobin saying the company hoped to run two LMP2s in the series next year. Morand Racing took another podium, the same three-car LMP2 podium as at Imola, which kept the team in the picture after its pointless start at Silverstone.
The next round of the season was the 3 Hours of Hungaroring on 14 September.

facts.v: Oliver Turvey's 1:23.871 in the Jota Zytek #38 stood as pole, ahead of the Murphy Oreca #18 on 1:24.010.
Signatech Alpine's fastest lap, a 1:23.737 from Nelson Panciatici, was set after a yellow flag; the stewards demoted the car to the back of the LMP2 field, and it started eighth.
The Murphy Oreca #18 failed to restart after its first routine stop and finished 25th, 20 laps down; a broken cable was blamed.
Jota was given a 30-second stop-go penalty at around half distance for the pit-lane speed limiter not working properly.
Thiriet by TDS Racing won two of the first three rounds and increased its championship lead.
